title: Vast
award: Site of the Day - Apr 1, 2026 (Honors, SOTD) - credits: Antinomy Studio
industry: Commercial space stations / aerospace hardware (Haven-1, Haven-2)
signature: A real space station you can handle in the browser: an R3F model of Haven-1 that you drag to rotate, switch between interior cutaway and exterior, and probe through 3D-anchored hotspots whose 30px squares clip-open into labels and photo callouts, plus a 360 interior walk-through whose jumps between panoramas use a barrel/pincushion warp shader, all inside a calm warm-neutral shell set in Owners.

first_screen.composition:
Full-bleed autoplay/muted/loop video (vast-public S3 '2026-03-13 Website Header_12MB.mp4', under a 10% dark overlay div) of the bright white cleanroom with the Haven-1 primary structure on a stand and technicians in white suits. Transparent nav on top at y~67: VAST wordmark at x=40, four links (Stations, Satellites, Updates, About us) spaced ~150px apart from x=282, then Shop and a white solid 'Create your mission' button (x 1218-1400, ~45px tall) on the right, all in white. The h1 (76px Owners 500, line-height 0.86) sits bottom-left at x=40 inside a 67rem (670px) max-width column, so its three authored lines ('Building
next-generation
space infrastructure') wrap to FOUR at 1440: 'space' ends line 3 alone and 'infrastructure' drops to line 4, under the cookie banner in desktop_00. The HTML puts a button group after the title in the same bottom-aligned flex row: a glass play/pause toggle and a boxed glass 'Watch full video' chevron button (YouTube trigger); both are hidden under the banner in the probe (position inferred bottom-right). No subline. In the probe the bottom ~20% is covered by the CookieYes banner (#ece8e3).
evidence: HTML .header-home__row-title{max-width:67rem}, .full-bg-video_dark-overlay opacity .1, .button-group in the hero row

motion.smooth_scroll: Lenis. html class 'lenis', globals.lenis true; bundle: new Lenis({autoRaf:false, lerp:.3, smoothWheel:true, syncTouch:false, prevent: cookie-preference panel}); lenis.raf driven from gsap.ticker with gsap.ticker.lagSmoothing(0). lerp .3 is fast, close to native feel.
motion.preloader: Not visible in the probe (desktop_00 is after a 6s settle). The bundle has a #loader with .loader-line/.loader-line-fill: the fill scales to load progress, finishes with scaleX 1 over .5s power2.inOut, then animates out (mobile: scaleY then scaleX over 1s). The same loader covers Barba page transitions.
motion.intro_sequence: Not observed. The earlier guess that the h1 is SplitText-staggered is unsupported: the bundle's only SplitText use is the statement fill ([data-split-text]). On a Barba enter, [data-hero-content] drops in from y -6rem while [data-hero-visual-wrap] scales 1.1->1 and its inner 1.2->1 (1.4s), defaults 1.25s 'animation-primary'.
scroll_techniques: scrub: scrub:0 on the statement fill (start '0% 60%', end '0% 10%') and the marquee drift; scrub:true on other pages' reveals (timeline dot #fff->#ff5623, image clip-path inset(0 20%)->inset(0) with scale 1.2->1); no pin anywhere in the bundle
word-by-word fill on the 48px statement: two stacked h2s (data-highlight main + an aria-hidden duplicate); the duplicate's words switch from opacity 0 to 1 one at a time

three-state nav: transparent over the video -> floating white inset bar after 100px -> hidden (y -100%, opacity 0, .7s power3.in) when scrolling down past one viewport height, back on scroll-up (.7s power3.out); delta threshold 50px
[data-parallax] elements offset by (distance from viewport centre) x speed on every Lenis scroll
horizontal drag carousels (data-drag) with square prev/next tiles; slide timeline .85s 'animation-primary' on xPercent
press-logo marquee: a linear xPercent loop whose timeScale flips sign with scroll direction (data-marquee-status normal/inverted) plus a scrub:0 x drift in vw across the section
motion.text_animation: Statement paragraph (verified in the bundle): SplitText splits both h2 copies into words (display:inline-flex, padding-bottom 2px). The base copy stays visible in asteroid-dust #897f75. Every word of the white duplicate starts at opacity 0 with transition: opacity .1s ease-out; one ScrollTrigger timeline (trigger the section, start '0% 60%', end '0% 10%', scrub:0) steps through the words (tween duration .1, stagger .01, expo.out) and each tween's onStart sets opacity 1 (onReverseComplete sets 0). So the fill is a per-word switch with a short CSS fade, not a gradient sweep. By desktop_01 all words are white.
motion.image_animation: 360 interior: panoramas change with a barrel/pincushion warp. Shader uniforms tMap, tMap2, uTextureProgress, uCenter; uv1 = barrelPincushion(scaleUV(vUv, c, map(p,0,1,1,0.4)), c, map(p,0,1,0,-8)); uv2 = barrelPincushion(scaleUV(vUv, c, map(p,0,1,1.6,1)), c, map(p,0,1,8,0)); color = mix(tex1, tex2, clamp(p*1.12,0,1)). uCenter.x is set to the clicked hotspot, tween defaults {ease:'power3.inOut', duration:.9}. Entering the immersive view: a full-screen 2x2 plane colored #E8E4DE whose top edge rises through a vertex shader (uRevealProgress, uFadeIn, uBendStrength), 1.6s power4.inOut to open and 1s to close, while the header animates out.
motion.page_transitions: Barba.js (@barba/core bundled; data-barba in the HTML), code-verified, not captured on video: beforeLeave adds html.loading; leave awaits loader.animateIn; enter sets the next container absolute with autoAlpha 0 and fades it in over .4s while the hero content drops from y -6rem and the hero visual scales 1.1->1 (inner 1.2->1, 1.4s); afterEnter runs loader.animateOut inside requestIdleCallback. The immersive-view wipe is a second, in-page transition.
hover_micro: Hotspots (bundle): a --callout-size 3rem (30px) square button whose clip-path polygon opens from the 30px square to the full label width on hover/open, with transform and clip-path transitions of calc(.3s * var(--motion)) on var(--motion-ease-vast), the cubic-bezier(.4,1.35,.5,.97) overshoot token; the button is scale-0 while its point is hidden. In frames/0 f03 the hovered square inverts to a white field with a dark core under a pointer cursor.

Callout card (bundle): title and image wipe in with a clip-path polygon from the bottom edge (polygon(0 100%,100% 100%,100% 100%,0 100%) -> full) and exit through the top edge, .7s power4.inOut. Mono uppercase title with a white square bullet that lands where the hotspot was, near-square photo (~1.1:1 in frames/0 f04, not 4:3).
Description boxes: 339px wide, min-height 206px, rgba(42,44,47,.27) + backdrop-blur 30px, 16px/1.16 copy (bundle Tailwind classes).

Buttons: two stacked layers, .btn-bg and .btn-wipe (#ece8e3 wipe over white, #000 over dark, 7% white over glass; glass bg = blur(2.8rem) + 10% white), plus a strip of four chevrons (.btn-icon-chevron-list) for a chevron roll; the hover motion itself was not captured.
Grab cursor over the 3D canvas while dragging (frames/0 f02, f05)
motion.cursor: Native. The 3D viewer switches to a grab hand; cursor:none is not used (css_usage.cursor_none 0).
easing_curves: cubic-bezier(0.62,0.05,0.01,0.99) (--animation-bezier; the same curve is registered as GSAP CustomEase 'animation-primary'; 9 CSS uses)
cubic-bezier(0.4,1.35,0.5,0.97) (--motion-ease-vast): drives the hotspot clip-path/transform transition and .gsap-scroll-bg opacity

linear(0, 0.007, 0.03 2.1%, 0.122 4.6%, 0.243 6.9% ...) (--motion-ease-spring): drives .gsap-scroll-item transforms (a fixed 4rem right-edge scroll rail defined in the embed CSS, not seen on the home screenshots)
GSAP: expo.out x32, sine.out x22, power3.inOut x8, 'animation-primary' x7, power3.out x4, power2.inOut x4, expo.inOut x4, power4.inOut x2
motion.duration_range_ms: CSS 150-550ms for UI (0.2s x9, 0.3s x8, 0.5s x7, 0.4s x5), 650ms primary (--animation-duration-primary .65s, fast .5s), 700ms-1s for larger moves. GSAP duration:1 x42, .3 x14, .5 x12, .4 x7, .7 x5 (nav hide/show, callout wipes), .85 carousel slides, 1.2 x4, 1.25 page enter, 1.6 for the immersive wipe.
motion.choreography_notes: The 3D viewer steps its chrome back: once you drag or zoom, the spec table, the HAVEN-1 label and the interior/exterior switch fade out and the camera moves in about 1.5x (the model grows from ~300 to ~460px tall between frames/0 f01 and f02). They come back when you zoom out (f06). In the immersive view the headline and button stay put while the panorama camera drifts; frames/1 f07 catches a hop mid-blend (two panoramas superimposed at different scales), consistent with the warp shader.
evidence: frames/0/f00-f07 (Haven-1 Interior & Exterior WebGL, 15.8s, frames at 0.99-14.78s)

three_d.stack: three.js r172 via React Three Fiber (React.createElement('planeGeometry'), drei-style shaderMaterial, makeDefault PerspectiveCamera), in a separate Vite bundle on CloudFront mounted into the Webflow page
three_d.role: product (Haven-1 exterior/interior cutaway with hotspots) plus a 360 interior world (panorama hops) and supporting models: a Dragon capsule docked to Haven-1 in the home Haven-1 section (desktop_02, not the hero), Haven-2 and an artificial-gravity station. desktop_02 also shows a figure in the porthole; inferred from the asset list: the haven1_low_poly_person / default_head GLBs.
three_d.materials_lighting_post: GLTFLoader with DRACOLoader, MeshoptDecoder and KTX2Loader in the bundle. The '-transformed.glb' suffix matches gltfjsx --transform output (Draco/Meshopt plus resized textures). MeshStandardMaterial (15 refs) and MeshPhysicalMaterial (6). RGBELoader loads two .hdr environments; solar_panel5.hdr is a panel-specific environment, which is why the arrays go from copper to dark blue cells as the model turns (frames/0 f02 vs f05). CubeCamera and WebGLRenderTarget are present. ACESFilmic/AgX/Neutral tone mapping exist in core; which one is active was not verified. Custom shaderMaterials for the panorama warp and the reveal plane. No EffectComposer or bloom string in the bundle; lighting reads soft, bright and studio-like.
three_d.interaction: Drag to rotate (grab cursor) with zoom-in; an 'INTERIOR [■] EXTERIOR' switch (mono labels either side of a small square knob on a moon-rock bar, frames/0 f01/f06); hotspots defined as data {title, paragraph, position:[x,y,z], uid, image:'/img/haven-demo/*.webp', side:'front'|'back'} (e.g. 'Deployable solar array' at [3.3,0,-.15], 'GNC', 'Radios'); a click opens a photo callout. 360 view: camera fov 80 at the origin with custom mousedown/touch drag handlers (no OrbitControls class in the bundle), idle look-around drift, and hotspot tags like 'CORRIDOR' (frames/1 f02) that jump to the next panorama through the warp shader.
three_d.performance_tactics: Device-tier classes on <html>: WEBGL_ENABLED only when DESKTOP && WEBGL_SUPPORTED && PERFORMANCE_GOOD, else WEBGL_DISABLED (bundle); IS_LOW_POWER_MODE comes from a hidden inline autoplay test video (class added if it stays paused after canplaythrough) and only affects the hero video; every React WebGL block ships a static render fallback (data-webgl-fb, e.g. 'Haven-1+Dragon ISO Full Frame' avif with png srcset); compressed '-transformed' GLBs; the gsap ticker drives one RAF for Lenis. The 3D payload is still 8.97MB declared on desktop.
three_d.fallback_mobile: inferred: a still image on phones. The tier logic disables WebGL off desktop and the HTML ships data-webgl-fb stills; mobile_01's station (no Dragon in view, a different angle from desktop_02) is consistent with that still. Not verified with a context count at 390px.
evidence: bundle grep: GLTFLoader x26, DRACOLoader x7, MeshoptDecoder x3, KTX2Loader x2, RGBELoader x5, CubeCamera x3, hotspot data objects, device-tier class logic

performance_accessibility.weight_notes: Heavy: hero mp4 11.46MB (the file name says 12MB), 3D 8.97MB, images ~4.1MB, custom JS bundle 1.54MB uncompressed plus Webflow/jQuery, and a long tail of ad and analytics hosts.
performance_accessibility.reduced_motion: 1 prefers-reduced-motion rule, and it is the switch: an inline embed sets :root{--motion:1} and @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce){:root{--motion:0}}; every CSS duration is calc(Xs * var(--motion)). The probe read --motion: 0, so the probe browser reported reduced motion. IS_LOW_POWER_MODE is unrelated (a JS autoplay test that only touches the hero video). GSAP tweens (nav, statement fill, callout wipes, panorama warp, reveal plane) do not read --motion; only CSS and the React Tailwind classes do.
performance_accessibility.contrast_issues: White 48px statement on moon-rock #b3aba3 is 2.27:1, below AA large (3:1); the base #897f75 words on #b3aba3 are 1.73:1. The white h1 over the bright cleanroom video has only a 10% dark overlay. The white 'Experience Haven-1 Interior' heading sits over near-white panorama walls with no scrim (frames/1). Orange #ff5623 cookie links on #ece8e3 are 2.6:1 at 14px. Mono 12px captions on translucent panels are small.
performance_accessibility.mobile_quality: Good: no horizontal overflow, 48px h1, the Haven-1 ring and station image render (likely the static fallback); the cookie sheet takes ~50% of the first mobile screen.

steal_this.technique: Hotspot product viewer with interior/exterior modes
steal_this.why_it_works: It turns a spec sheet into something you can hold: the visitor drags the real product, flips to a cutaway, and gets photo proof at each part, so trust comes from the hardware itself.
steal_this.how_to_build: R3F + drei. Run the models through `npx gltfjsx model.glb --transform` (Draco/Meshopt, resized textures) and load with useGLTF. Add an RGBE .hdr environment for reflections and give the solar arrays their own env map (Vast loads solar_panel5.hdr beside hdr5.hdr) so they swing copper to blue as they turn. Controls: the bundle has no OrbitControls class, so write a small damped drag-rotate or use OrbitControls (enablePan false, enableDamping); show a grab cursor while dragging. Keep hotspots as data {title, paragraph, position:[x,y,z], image, side:'front'|'back'} (Vast: 'Deployable solar array' at [3.3,0,-.15]). Render each with drei <Html position> as a 30px (3rem) button: background rgba(42,44,47,.27), backdrop-filter blur(30px), a 10px white square inside, clip-path polygon(0 0,30px 0,30px 30px,0 30px) that opens to polygon(0 0,100% 0,100% 100%,0 100%) on hover to reveal the label, transition clip-path and transform .3s cubic-bezier(.4,1.35,.5,.97); invert to a white field with a dark core on hover; scale(0) when the point faces away (inferred test: dot(normal, cameraDir) per side). On click open a callout at the hotspot: a mono uppercase title whose white square bullet sits on the hotspot, and a near-square photo, wiped in with clip-path from polygon(0 100%,100% 100%,100% 100%,0 100%) to the full box over .7s power4.inOut and out through the top edge. inferred (not in the bundle): on drag/zoom fade the spec table and switch to opacity 0 and dolly the camera ~1.5x; the switch swaps the cutout GLB and the full body.

steal_this.why_it_works: Moving between 360 nodes feels like walking forward through the doorway instead of a crossfade, and it only costs one fragment shader.
steal_this.how_to_build: PerspectiveCamera fov 80 at [0,0,0] (makeDefault) inside an inverted sphere or a fullscreen quad sampling the panoramas. ShaderMaterial uniforms tMap, tMap2, uTextureProgress (p), uCenter (vec2, default (.25,.5)). Fragment, as shipped: vec2 bp(vec2 uv, vec2 c, float s){vec2 st=uv-c; return c+(1.+s*dot(st,st))*st;} uv1=bp(c+(vUv-c)*mix(1.,.4,p), c, -8.*p); uv2=bp(c+(vUv-c)*mix(1.6,1.,p), c, 8.*(1.-p)); gl_FragColor=vec4(mix(texture2D(tMap,uv1).rgb, texture2D(tMap2,uv2).rgb, clamp(p*1.12,0.,1.)),1.) (SCALE_AMOUNT .6, PINCUSHION_STRENGTH 8). On a hotspot click: inferred, set uCenter.x from the tag's screen x; tMap=current; tMap2=next; p=0; gsap.to(u.uTextureProgress,{value:1, duration:.9, ease:'power3.inOut'}).

steal_this.technique: Ghost wordmark behind a transparent WebGL object
steal_this.why_it_works: The product name becomes the backdrop, so the name and the object register in one glance, and because the contrast is only tonal the model stays the hero.
steal_this.how_to_build: <h2> at font-size 24vw (345.6px at 1440), line-height 1, color #ece8e3 on #fdfcf4 (1.2:1, a tonal step). Put a transparent R3F canvas (gl={{alpha:true}}) absolutely on top, centred. Behind the model add the ring: Vast ships it as one baked SVG path (viewBox 609x611) of ~116 short radial ticks, 6 units long and under 1 unit wide; the same look comes from <circle r='300' fill='none' stroke='currentColor' stroke-width='6' stroke-dasharray='0.5 15.75'/> in a warm grey, plus one ~40px #ff5623 tick at 12 o'clock. Keep the h2 real text for SEO (Vast renders a second xs--show copy for phones) and put a still render behind the canvas as the no-WebGL fallback. On mobile the word still spans the width (~25vw).

steal_this.technique: One motion multiplier token shared by CSS and GSAP
steal_this.why_it_works: Reduced motion and low-power handling become a single switch, and the CSS and JS curves cannot drift apart.
steal_this.how_to_build: :root{--motion:1; --animation-bezier:cubic-bezier(.62,.05,.01,.99); --animation-primary:calc(.65s * var(--motion)) var(--animation-bezier); --animation-primary-fast:calc(.5s * var(--motion)) var(--animation-bezier);} @media (prefers-reduced-motion:reduce){:root{--motion:0}}. Use transition: transform var(--animation-primary). In JS: CustomEase.create('animation-primary','0.62, 0.05, 0.01, 0.99'); Vast's GSAP tweens ignore --motion, so do better: read getComputedStyle(root).getPropertyValue('--motion') and skip or jump tweens when it is 0. Device tiers as Vast does them: add WEBGL_ENABLED only when DESKTOP && WEBGL_SUPPORTED && PERFORMANCE_GOOD (else WEBGL_DISABLED), detect low-power mode with a hidden muted autoplay test <video> (still paused after canplaythrough = IS_LOW_POWER_MODE), and give every WebGL block a static still (data-webgl-fb) shown under WEBGL_DISABLED.

steal_this.technique: Full-screen vertex-shader wipe into an immersive mode
steal_this.why_it_works: Opening the 360 view feels like entering the station: a warm sheet rises from the bottom, the header leaves, and the panorama is underneath.
steal_this.how_to_build: In the same R3F scene, render planeGeometry args [2,2,1,1] with depthTest and depthWrite off and a vertex shader that skips the projection: vec3 pos=position; if(uFadeIn){ if(pos.y>0.) pos.y -= (1.-uRevealProgress)*2.; } else { if(pos.y<1.) pos.y += (1.-uRevealProgress)*2.; } gl_Position=modelMatrix*vec4(pos,1.) (with an identity modelMatrix that is clip space). Fragment is a flat uColor #E8E4DE. Open: gsap.to(u.uRevealProgress,{value:1,duration:1.6,ease:'power4.inOut'}); close: to 0, duration 1. The leading edge is straight: Vast passes uBendStrength:0 and defines PI, but its shader never reads them. For a curved edge add x segments (args [2,2,32,1]) and pos.y += sin((pos.x*.5+.5)*PI)*uBend. Animate the header out at the same time.

steal_this.technique: Fast Lenis on the GSAP ticker
steal_this.why_it_works: lerp .3 smooths wheel steps without the floaty lag that heavy smooth-scroll adds, and one RAF keeps ScrollTrigger and WebGL in sync.
steal_this.how_to_build: const lenis = new Lenis({autoRaf:false, lerp:.3, smoothWheel:true, syncTouch:false, prevent: el => el.closest('.cookie-panel')}); lenis.on('scroll', ScrollTrigger.update); gsap.ticker.add(t => lenis.raf(t*1000)); gsap.ticker.lagSmoothing(0).

steal_this.technique: Three-state header: transparent, floating island, hidden
steal_this.why_it_works: The hero keeps a clean full-bleed frame, the reading sections get a solid inset bar, and the bar gets out of the way while you read downward.
steal_this.how_to_build: On each Lenis scroll compare targetScroll with the last value and act only on moves of 50px or more. Past 100px add a 'started' state: the nav becomes a white bar inset 28px from the edges, 80px tall, soft tight shadow, ink text. Scrolling down past one viewport height (innerHeight, recomputed on resize) hides it with gsap.to('nav',{y:'-100%',opacity:0,duration:.7,ease:'power3.in'}); any upward move brings it back with {y:0,opacity:1,duration:.7,ease:'power3.out'}. Keep it shown while the menu is open. Put the shadow on the same element you hide, or its shadow is left behind as a band along the top edge (Vast's scrolled screenshots show one).

slop_risks: Cream/beige editorial background: the page base is #fdfcf4 warm-white, #ece8e3 warm-gray and #b3aba3 moon-rock. Vast earns it with geology-named tokens and a space-hardware subject; a naive copy is oat milk.

Saturated accent pop, and the little filled dot before an eyebrow: solar orange #ff5623 squares sit between 'PRESS RELEASE' and each date. It works here because orange appears nowhere else; spread onto buttons or headline words it becomes the template tell.

Monospace as the house voice / one label treatment: Phonic uppercase covers dates, categories, spec tables, carousel captions and link labels ('SEE THE MANUFACTURING AND TESTING'). Data use is legitimate; captions and links stretch it into a costume.

Text you cannot read: white 48px statement on #b3aba3 at 2.27:1, and the base words at #897f75 are 1.73:1; the white 'Experience Haven-1 Interior' heading sits on near-white panorama walls with no scrim.

Scroll-stepped word-by-word text fill is a heavily copied trope. Copy it only if the base state is fully readable; Vast's base copy (#897f75 on #b3aba3, 1.73:1) is not, so until you scroll the statement reads as disabled text.

Standard corporate lower half: 3-column news cards, press-logo marquee, a 'Sign up for updates' field-plus-button row and link columns under mono uppercase labels. The field and button are square (not the email-pill form), and the footer is an inset island on black without a giant wordmark or copyright row, so it avoids the worst of the standard footer, but the field-plus-button newsletter row itself is still the stock move.

Multi-line headline: the h1's column is capped at 67rem, so at 1440 'Building / next-generation / space / infrastructure' stacks four lines with 'space' stranded alone. Set the width so the authored three lines hold, or cut the line.

Image card with overlay caption: carousel photos carry a translucent panel with a small mono uppercase label, a bullet and a description, the same anatomy as the overlay-caption card preset. The blur panel is better than a gradient scrim, but the pattern repeats on every slide.
Unrounded hairline rules as decoration: the 1px vertical rules between press quotes.
Weight: a 12MB hero loop plus 9MB of GLBs on the home page. A copy without device tiering stalls on mid-range phones.

Botched shadow leak: when the floating nav hides, a ~25px shadow band stays across the top of the viewport (x 28-1412) in the scrolled screenshots (desktop_02, desktop_04-07). Observed; the cause is inferred (the shadow lives on an element that is not hidden with the bar).
